intention: Persist the full Game Design Doc for Santa Cap Catcher before any scene construction, so the construction gate accepts edit_by_dsl.

scene_representation.decision_summary: Live camera feed stays full-screen as the backdrop (composition none). Gameplay is a screen-space 2D layer at 720x1280 with falling hat items and edge HUD. A Head Tracker rig supplies a forehead anchor whose world position is projected to screen pixels each frame, so the catcher collider follows the user's real forehead without moving the camera feed.

space.description: 720x1280 screen space for all gameplay items and HUD, layered directly over the camera feed.

content_form.description: Flat 2D sprites, art text and a soft radial forehead ring, plus 3D camera and head tracker rig underneath.

requirements.description: The catcher hit point tracks the user's real forehead position every frame and mirrors head movement horizontally and vertically.
The live camera feed stays visible and unobstructed in the center of the screen during calibration, gameplay and result.
Every caught or missed item produces immediate visible feedback (pop burst, score number, red flash and shake) and a matching sound.
All HUD text and the retry button stay inside the TikTok safe zone so nothing is clipped by the TikTok UI.

layers.description: Main Camera plus Head Tracker; an Empty child at forehead height supplies the world-space anchor that is projected to screen pixels.

space.description: 3D camera space driven by head tracking

content_form.description: Tracking anchor transform only, no visible mesh

layers.description: 2D Camera canvas holding the forehead ring, pooled falling hat items, gold gifts and bad bombs that spawn at the top and fall to the bottom.

content_form.description: Flat sprite quads positioned by script

layers.description: Score, miss icons, timer bar, countdown art text, calibration prompt and the translucent result card with retry button, all anchored to safe-zone edges.

content_form.description: Flat art text, labels and translucent panels

layers.description: Full-screen camera feed rendered behind every 2D layer, never covered by an opaque panel.

limitations: Hit detection uses distance in projected screen pixels, not true 3D depth, so an item is caught when its 2D distance to the projected forehead point is small.
Without a detected face the forehead anchor falls back to screen center so the game stays playable in the editor preview.

verification.description: Move the preview head horizontally and vertically, then compare the ring position with the head tracker.
verification.success_criteria: The ring follows the forehead in the same direction with no visible lag or drift.

verification.description: Screenshot calibration, gameplay and result screens and confirm the face region is unobstructed.
verification.success_criteria: The center of the frame shows the live camera feed at all times with no opaque full-screen panel.

verification.description: Trigger a normal catch, a gold catch and a bad catch and inspect the pop text, burst, red flash and shake.
verification.success_criteria: Score popup and burst appear within one frame of contact and a miss flashes red with a screen shake.

verification.description: Inspect the layout bounds of every HUD element and the retry button against the safe zone.
verification.success_criteria: All HUD items sit within x -340..260 and y -400..500.

starter_template.rationale: The closest strong buildable, chef_hat_catch, steers a pot by dragging and ends on a timer only. This design is head-tracked with a forehead collider, weighted item mix, consecutive-miss and cumulative-miss loss, and a speed ramp, so the scaffold's drag input would have to be ripped out. Built from scratch while borrowing its falling-item stream and HUD framing.

interactions.response: Reset score to 0, misses to 0, consecutive misses to 0, timer to 45, speed to base, clear all falling items, show CalibrationScreen and hide GameplayScreen and ResultScreen.

interactions.trigger: Forehead anchor held within 90 px of the red calibration line for 0.6 s
interactions.response: Play the countdown 3-2-1-GO on the gameplay screen, then begin spawning falling hats.

feedback.visual: Calibration line turns green and pulses, countdown art text pops in the center

interactions.trigger: Falling item overlaps the projected forehead ring point
interactions.response: Normal hat adds 1 point, gold gift adds 3 points and raises spawn speed, bad bomb subtracts 2 points and adds one miss; the item is recycled to the pool.

feedback.visual: Item pops with a golden star burst, art-text score popup rises above the ring, HUD score bumps

interactions.trigger: A bad bomb touches the forehead ring and on every item that falls past the bottom edge uncaught
interactions.response: Add one miss, shake the camera, flash the screen red and update the miss icons; reaching 10 total misses or 5 consecutive misses ends the round immediately.
interactions.state_change: PLAYING -> RESULT when the miss limit is hit

feedback.visual: Red translucent screen flash plus a short camera shake and a shrinking miss icon

interactions.response: Hide GameplayScreen, show ResultScreen with the final score, rank title, share copy and duet copy.

feedback.visual: Result card scales in with a soft glow while remaining camera feed stays visible

interactions.response: Reset score, misses, consecutive misses and timer, clear the item pool and return to the calibration screen.

feedback.visual: Retry button punch-scale and the result card slides out

assets.description: Cartoon red santa hat with white fur trim and a pompom, glossy storybook style, centered on transparent background, ready to fall down the screen.
Golden santa cap with sparkles and a small gift box ribbon, shiny metallic highlights, bonus item worth three points, centered on transparent background.
Grumpy green monster holding a round black bomb with a lit fuse, clearly readable as a bad item, centered on transparent background for the falling item stream.
Soft golden ring with a glowing inner gradient and a small star marker at the center, no hard edges, sized to read as a catch hit area over the camera feed.
Single soft white six-point snowflake with gentle blur, semi-transparent, used many times at different sizes for drifting snow over the camera feed.
Radial golden star burst with sharp four-point sparkles and a warm glow, transparent background, played once when a hat is caught for hit feedback.
Rounded dark red translucent pill plate with a thin gold border and subtle candy stripe, used behind the score and miss icons so text stays readable over the feed.
Small hollow gold star outline that fills with dull grey when a miss is used, matching the cute festive HUD style, used five times in the miss icon row.
Translucent deep red rounded card with gold snowflake border and soft inner vignette, sized to cover the middle of the screen without hiding the whole camera feed.
Rounded bright red button plate with a gold rim and glossy highlight, sized for a two hundred forty by eighty retry button at the bottom of the result card.
Curated decorative art text with heavy gradient fill and outline, reused for the 3-2-1-GO countdown, the START banner and the score popup moment.
Curated arcade style art text with lit outline and glow, reused for the title on the calibration screen and the TIME UP banner on the result screen.
Upbeat original chiptune holiday loop with sleigh bells and bells melody, about thirty seconds, looped for the whole session.
Short bright bell tick used once per countdown number and reused as the retry button click sound.
Crisp pop and jingle chime played whenever a normal or golden hat lands inside the forehead ring.
Short muffled explosion with a descending buzz played on a bad bomb catch and on any uncaught item falling off screen.
Two second festive fanfare with bells and a rising chord played when the result card reveals the final score and rank.

random_behaviors.range: 65 percent normal cap, 15 percent golden gift, 20 percent bad bomb
random_behaviors.verify_strategy: Force spawn 20 items in preview and log the type counts, confirm the split is within 15 percent of the target weights.

random_behaviors.range: uniform random x between -280 and 260 in screen space
random_behaviors.verify_strategy: Capture three gameplay screenshots and confirm every spawned item starts within the horizontal safe bounds.

random_behaviors.what: fall speed after each five correct catches
random_behaviors.range: plus 10 percent of the base speed per five catches, capped at 1.8 times base
random_behaviors.verify_strategy: Log the speed multiplier after every fifth catch and confirm it ramps 1.0 to 1.1 to 1.2 and stops at 1.8.

camera_feed_constraints.tracking_range: full screen; the face stays visible in the center band while HUD elements hug the top and bottom safe-zone edges

mechanic.description: Head-tracked catching game: pooled hats, golden gifts and bad bombs fall from the top of the screen and the user catches the good ones with a forehead ring projected from the head tracker. Weighted item mix, speed ramp every five catches, and loss on ten total misses or five consecutive misses.

criteria.check: Score counter sits top-left, five miss icons top-right and the timer bar above them, all inside the safe zone.
No opaque full-screen panel covers the camera feed on any of the three screens; the result card is translucent.
RecordStart resets score, misses, timer and item pool and returns to the calibration screen.
Holding the head on the red line for 0.6 seconds starts the 3-2-1-GO countdown and then playing.
Ten total misses or five consecutive misses ends the round immediately with the result screen.
The retry button returns to calibration with a fully reset game state.
Normal hat is plus one, golden gift is plus three with a thirty percent speed boost, bad bomb is minus two and counts one miss.
Each five correct catches raises the global fall speed by ten percent up to one point eight times the base speed.
The round always ends at forty five seconds even if no miss limit is reached.
Score never drops below zero and the miss icon row never shows fewer than zero icons.
Spawned item types follow the sixty five fifteen twenty weighting over a sample of twenty spawns.
The camera feed stays visible and the foreground never hides the whole face region.
A catch produces a golden star burst and a rising art-text score popup, a miss flashes red with a screen shake.
